expectations.text: Chooses EditMode tests (not PlayMode) because DamageCalculator is pure C# logic with no Unity lifecycle
expectations.evidence: Response states in the test file's header comment: 'No MonoBehaviour or scene loading required — pure C# logic.' and the section 'What was produced' describes the class as a pure logic component. The choice of EditMode is consistent throughout with no PlayMode assembly or [UnityTest] used.

expectations.text: Creates or describes a test assembly definition (.asmdef) that references the production Gameplay assembly and nunit.framework.dll, with includePlatforms set to Editor
expectations.evidence: Project.Gameplay.Tests.asmdef is shown with: "references": ["Project.Gameplay", "UnityEngine.TestRunner", "UnityEditor.TestRunner"], "includePlatforms": ["Editor"], and "precompiledReferences": ["nunit.framework.dll"]. Annotated: 'restricts to EditMode only' and 'ensures NUnit is linked'.

Every test method uses [Test] or [TestCase]. For example: '[Test] public void Calculate_AttackExceedsDefense_ReturnsPositiveDamage()' and '[TestCase(0f, 0f, 1f, 0f, TestName = "Boundary_AllZero")]'. No [UnityTest] attributes appear in the file.

expectations.text: Tests follow Arrange-Act-Assert structure with descriptive names like Method_ExpectedBehavior_WhenCondition
expectations.evidence: Most tests are one-liners with no explicit Arrange/Act/Assert sections (e.g., 'float result = _calc.Calculate(attackPower: 100f, defense: 40f, criticalMultiplier: 1f); Assert.That(result, Is.EqualTo(60f).Within(0.001f));' — no Arrange step, no comments separating phases). Additionally, names follow the pattern Method_Condition_Result (e.g., 'Calculate_AttackExceedsDefense_ReturnsPositiveDamage') rather than the specified Method_ExpectedBehavior_WhenCondition pattern. Borderline cases like 'Calculate_CriticalMultiplier_ScalesDamage' omit the 'When' clause entirely.

expectations.text: Assertions use NUnit constraint syntax such as Assert.That(x, Is.EqualTo(y))
expectations.evidence: Uses constraint syntax throughout: 'Assert.That(result, Is.EqualTo(60f).Within(0.001f))' and 'Assert.That(ex.ParamName, Is.EqualTo("attackPower"))'. Exception tests use Assert.Throws<T> which is also NUnit constraint-compatible.

expectations.text: Explains how to run the tests from the command line with Unity -batchmode -runTests -testPlatform EditMode -testResults, or via scripts/run_unity_tests.py
expectations.evidence: Shows the batchmode command: '/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/<UnityVersion>/Unity.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity -batchmode -runTests -testPlatform EditMode -projectPath /tmp/eval-work/dmg-b -testResults /tmp/eval-work/dmg-b/TestResults.xml -logFile /tmp/eval-work/dmg-b/unity.log -quit'. All required flags (-batchmode, -runTests, -testPlatform EditMode, -testResults) are present. No mention of scripts/run_unity_tests.py, but the assertion allows 'or via scripts/run_unity_tests.py' as an alternative.
